summary.headline: Sell measurable security and admin fixes as narrow services; validate paid demand before building SaaS.
summary.best_opportunity: Cyber-hygiene setup and ongoing readiness for UK micro-businesses
summary.why_now: The live UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 reports 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack, and only 9% of micro-businesses were aware of Cyber Essentials. This establishes a real gap, not willingness to buy a specific consultant; test with paid diagnostics.

top_opportunities.name: Cyber-hygiene and Cyber Essentials readiness for micro-businesses
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope baseline, MFA/backup/email configuration checks, action plan and monthly evidence/reminder support; refer certification work to qualified partners where required.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 says 43% of businesses had a breach or attack and just 9% of micro-businesses knew of Cyber Essentials. Awareness gap suggests need, but buyer demand and conversion remain unproven.
top_opportunities.buyer: UK micro-businesses handling customer data, especially small professional practices and suppliers to larger firms
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for basic tooling, insurance research and outreach; avoid offering assurance beyond competence.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if a paid baseline is sold directly; estimate, not observed result.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £50–£200/month for checks, staff refreshers and evidence upkeep; validate retention.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit for a software engineer if scope stays to practical configuration and referral, not formal certification or penetration testing.
risks: Security work carries liability; competence, insurance and clear scope are essential.
Survey prevalence does not prove budget or willingness to hire a small provider.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best evidence-led service to test: sell a modest baseline first and stay within demonstrable competence.

top_opportunities.name: AI enquiry-to-booking automation for one home-service niche
top_opportunities.description: Connect existing website forms, email and calendar to acknowledge, qualify and route enquiries, with human approval and monthly monitoring.
top_opportunities.why_now: The operational value is easy to demonstrate through response-time and booking metrics, but live evidence retrieved this run did not establish tradespeople's buying intent; validate via paid pilots.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent plumbers, electricians and other appointment-based trades
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£700 using existing hardware and low-cost automation services.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks with direct sales and a paid pilot; unverified estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £100–£400/month support and workflow tuning; willingness to pay unverified.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical delivery fit; narrow integrations can be reused.
risks: Crowded automation market; generic positioning is weak.
Customer data, consent and unreliable AI outputs require safeguards and human fallback.
top_opportunities.verdict: Test one trade-specific outcome; do not build a platform before deposits.

top_opportunities.name: SME invoice-chasing and payment-status automation
top_opportunities.description: Automate polite reminders, payment-status tracking and escalation from an SME's existing accounting workflow; keep a human in control of disputes.
top_opportunities.why_now: Late payment is a longstanding SME cash-flow pain, but this run could not retrieve a fresh authoritative 2026 signal. Treat demand as a hypothesis and validate with local firms.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small B2B agencies, consultancies and subcontractors with recurring overdue invoices
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–4 weeks if sold as an implementation; estimate only.
risks: Accounting software may already provide reminders.
Payment disputes and customer relationships make fully automatic chasing risky.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell a time-saving integration, not another standalone invoicing app.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business website care and conversion fixes
top_opportunities.description: A fixed-price cleanup of speed, mobile usability, enquiry forms and analytics followed by a simple monthly maintenance plan.
top_opportunities.why_now: Low-cost, observable improvements can be sold locally, but current evidence of a UK-wide demand surge was not established in this run.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local service businesses with outdated sites and measurable enquiry flows
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks for a paid audit or repair; estimate.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for a software engineer able to ship fixes quickly.
risks: Maintenance can become unbounded without strict scope.
top_opportunities.verdict: A practical fallback when prospects have clear site defects; productize scope and support limits.

top_opportunities.name: AI workflow audit and implementation for small professional firms
top_opportunities.description: Map one repetitive admin workflow, automate a bounded part, document controls and report time saved; charge for discovery and delivery separately.
top_opportunities.why_now: Interest in AI is not equivalent to procurement; no fresh buyer-intent evidence was verified in this run. A workflow audit can expose concrete ROI before implementation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small accountancy, recruitment and legal-adjacent firms with repetitive back-office work
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–4 weeks; depends on trust and procurement.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £150–£500/month for support and iteration, subject to demonstrated value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong engineering fit, with added need for domain understanding and change management.
risks: Sensitive data and hallucinations require strict access, testing and human review.
Broad AI consulting is crowded and can be hard to differentiate.
top_opportunities.verdict: Choose one workflow and one industry; price against measured hours saved.

best_pick.name: Cyber-hygiene and Cyber Essentials readiness for micro-businesses
best_pick.why_it_wins: It has the strongest current evidence in this run: official 2025 survey results show substantial breach prevalence and low micro-business awareness of Cyber Essentials. A bounded diagnostic can be sold before any software build, while monthly upkeep offers a recurring service path. Evidence supports the problem, not guaranteed sales.
validation_plan: Interview 10 local micro-business owners about recent security checks, buyer triggers and existing IT support; record actual objections and current spend.
Offer a paid, fixed-scope baseline to 3 prospects; proceed only if at least one pays and the work is within your competence and insured scope.
best_pick.first_offer: £199 fixed-price, 90-minute cyber-hygiene baseline plus prioritized written actions; no certification claim, penetration test or guarantee.
best_pick.mvp: A repeatable checklist, secure evidence-handling process and concise action-plan template; use manual delivery before building software.
customer_types: Micro-business suppliers seeking to demonstrate basic security readiness
best_pick.do_today: Review the GOV.UK 2025 survey, define your exact competence boundary and draft a one-page £199 pilot offer; contact five relevant local firms for discovery conversations.
